title: This Animal Sees Without Lenses and Outlived the Dinosaurs
subject: chambered nautilus

scenes.text: This animal sees with no lens, and it outlived the dinosaurs.
The chambered nautilus has barely changed in about 500 million years.
Its eyes are simple pinholes, like the first cameras. They catch light and shadow, not sharp pictures.
By day it hides in dark water down to about 2,000 feet. At night it rises to feed.
Gas-filled chambers in its shell work like submarine tanks. It adds more as it grows, from four to about thirty.
Blurry eyes, a submarine shell, and five mass extinctions survived. Not bad for a pinhole.

description:
This animal sees with no lens, and it outlived the dinosaurs.
The chambered nautilus has a pinhole eye and a shell that works like a submarine.
What other living fossil should we cover?
first_comment: Pinhole eyes and still alive after five mass extinctions. What living fossil should we cover next?
